facts.text: Kerem HaTeimanim was founded in 1906 by Yemenite‑Jewish immigrants on land owned by Aharon Chelouche, Yosef Moyal, and Haim Amzaleg.
Known as the Yemenite Quarter, the neighborhood sits between the bustling Carmel Market and the Mediterranean Sea, blending old‑world charm with beachfront access.
In 2004, the Lev HaIr Tower became Kerem HaTeimanim’s tallest building, marking a modern architectural milestone in the area.
The early 1970s saw the formation of the Sounds of the Vineyard Band, a local group that gained fame beyond south Tel Aviv.
In the 1980s, Yemenite‑Israeli singer Zohar Argov released an album titled “Bekerem Hateymanim,” celebrating the neighborhood’s cultural significance.
Kerem HaTeimanim is a culinary hotspot, hosting everything from classic falafel joints to upscale fusion kitchens that rival any other Tel Aviv neighborhood.
